data.abstract: Power transformer maintenance is critical to electricity utilities. Transformer failure results in electricity outages and replacement costs. In this study, both qualitative and quantitative research methods were used to determine maintenance factors which contribute to transformer failures. Semi-structured interviews and archival data collection methods were used. A total of 10 participants within the transformer maintenance field were interviewed and 30 previous transformer investigation failure reports were analysed in terms of their direct and root cause of failures. The aim of this research was to investigate the impact of inadequate transformer maintenance on transformer failures. It was found that skills, training and failure to follow maintenance procedures are some of the critical factors that contribute to inadequate transformer maintenance. Investment in the continuous training of maintenance personnel and the use of online monitoring diagnostic tools, will improve maintenance, which will reduce unplanned cost due to transformer failure.

data.abstract: : Asset Management assists in operating electrical utilities at high performance and low cost. The Power Transformer Health Index (PTHI) is considered a good health condition evaluation and decision-making tool. PTHI is used to prioritize maintenance decisions, drive maintenance strategy, manage failure impact before it occurs, asset lifecycle planning, deferral big capitals, manage spare parts plan, and extend power transformer life. This paper presents the PTHI models’ investigation which was conducted on 4324 transformer records using various Artificial Intelligent Machine Learning (ML) algorithms: Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naïve Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF) and k-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) in R programming language. Several evaluation metrics present comparable analyses using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. According to the results, the SVM model was found applicable to local electrical utility transformers' health condition assessment. The paper addressed integrating international best practices and AM into the HI model.

data.abstract: This study reviews the historical maintenance records (2012~2024) and the operational challenges of the IEC61850-based Digital Control Systems (DCS), also known as Substation Automation Systems (SAS), deployed within our utility. Given the early adoption of IEC 61850 (first DCS installed in 2006), we assess the initial challenges and defects caused by limited understanding of the protocol, alongside the continuous improvements made over time. Our analysis revealed that about half of the maintenance activities of the systems were attributable to the server and gateway failures, underscoring the need for a more robust solution. In response, this study focuses on integrating IEC61850-compliant Remote Terminal Units (IRTU) as a replacement. A series of testing phases, including laboratory simulations and real-world trial runs at a newly constructed substation, demonstrated that IRTUs significantly improve system reliability, availability, and maintainability. The findings reveal that IRTUs offer notable enhancements in operational efficiency, energy efficiency, and cybersecurity, making them a promising solution for long-term sustainability in substation automation. During the IRTU integration process, we identified an opportunity to standardize the electrical schematic diagrams and adopt the IEC 61850 protocol to replace traditional hardwiring interlocks. This addresses high failure rates of auxiliary wiring and components, often resulting in remote control failures, loss of signaling, and prolonged construction times. This paper outlines the benefits and performance improvements resulting from this transition, highlighting key areas for further enhancement in operations.

data.abstract: Abstract This article presents an analysis of 343 distribution and power transformer component failures in the voltage range of 33 kV–400 kV over an operational period of 11 years from Tamil Nadu Electric Utility (TNEU), India. Two methods were employed in this study. Initially, failure data were analyzed using statistical analysis and grouped into four major failure level which includes electrical, thermal, mechanical and insulation degradation. Further, causes of failure were also identified through maintenance records, direct observations in repair yard and expert consultations. Subsequently, a Health Index (HI) approach to transformer maintenance has been proposed for implementation. By adopting this approach, a case study was presented where a health index was calculated for seven power transformers. The results of HI were used for maintenance decisions such as: should the transformer continue in service, be repaired, be refurbished, or be replaced. This study provides a practical guidance to maintenance personnel for early fault diagnosis that prevents unexpected failure of in-service power transformers and reduce maintenance cost in electric utilities.
